title: Horse Noises
blurb: Enormous, emotionally volatile, and sounding exactly like that. A horse in full vocal expression — neighing, snorting, and communicating a level of feeling entirely disproportionate to whatever prompted it — remains one of the most dramatic noises any animal produces. Cinema has leaned on it for a century, usually to signal that a scene has turned. Play it for cowboy edits, for unexpected arrivals, or for any situation where the only appropriate response left available to you is simply a horse. No further explanation has ever been required.
